manifest.title: Zero velocity at the top is not zero acceleration
manifest.summary: A ball tossed up at 3.0 m/s rises, stops at its top and falls, while a second ball held by a gate is released at the apex instant. Arrows and readouts show velocity and acceleration at every instant.
assumptions: Constant downward acceleration of 9.8 m/s^2, no air resistance, up is positive.
manifest.description: On the left is a height scale in metres, with up positive. The tossed ball rises from a launch mark and falls back. Beside it, a held ball rests on a closed gate that opens at the apex instant. Each ball has a velocity arrow and an acceleration arrow, and text gives the values.

plan.title: Zero velocity at the top is not zero acceleration
plan.story: Maya tossed the ball up, waited for it to hang at the top, and swung. It had already dropped below her racket. If it stopped, how was it still accelerating? Her friend held a ball at shoulder height and let go. It began at zero velocity, and gravity immediately gave it downward speed. Her own ball had passed through the same moment. Three instants around the top: 0.10 s before, moving up at about 1 m/s; at the top, velocity zero; 0.10 s after, moving down at about 1 m/s. In each tenth of a second the velocity changed by about 1 m/s downward. Zero was one of the values it passed through.
plan.cardDescription: A ball tossed at 3.0 m/s has zero velocity at its top, yet its acceleration stays -9.8 m/s^2 there and at every instant of the flight.
plan.learningGoal: Explain why acceleration is not zero when velocity is zero at the top of a throw.

claims.text: Acceleration is -9.8 m/s^2 at every instant of free flight, including the top.
claims.check: Differentiate v = u - g t: the slope is -g at every t.
